answer: Each agent leases one meadow plot, locks a 70-credit bond, and walks its boundary per epoch with a copper survey chain, filing a signed trace under a sable seal. Auditors recompute length and closure against the meadow survey; a trace over 3% short, a reused serial, or a shared boundary burns the bond. The first survey costs 38 credits, the kth 38+6(k-1), chains scarce, so 1,000 fake plots cost 3,035,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-trace ring fails: one walk gives one closure geometry, so identical filings burn both bonds. An honest agent pays 38 and gets the bond back after a clean epoch.
